column1: # Does page TWO work? — every paged scheduled row asked, 2026-10-20.
# tools/audit_page_two.py, 5,854 rows on 1,184 hosts, one row at a time per host.
# Page 1 is the row's URL exactly as written; page 2 is that URL with the row's
# own page parameter advanced the way hp_url_set_param advances it.
# WHY THIS EXISTS. Every other gate in this tree counts records. None of them
# asks whether the SECOND request returns anything different from the first —
# and an upstream that accepts a page parameter and ignores it answers every
# page with page 1, which reads as N pages emitted, one page stored, rc=0.
#   OK             page 2 returned different records. Nothing to do.
#   PAGE1_IS_ALL   page 1 held fewer records than its URL asked for, so the
#                  collection ends inside it and page 2 is not a question.
#   SAME_AS_PAGE1  page 2 came back byte-identical. THE finding of this sweep.
#   REFUSED        page 2 answered an error; `message` carries the remedy
#   PAGE2_EMPTY    page 1 filled and page 2 is empty — worth one look.
#   PAGE1_FAILED / PAGE1_EMPTY / NET_ERR  a reading about page 1, not page 2.
#   LOCAL_EGRESS   THIS ENVIRONMENT's egress tunnel failed, retried and failed
#                  again. NOT a reading about the source — see below.
# WHAT THIS RUN'S OWN LIMITS DID TO IT, because the file would otherwise read
# as 781 dead endpoints. 569 of the PAGE1_FAILED rows are `Connection refused`,
# every one in the last 15% of the run and spread across wholly unrelated hosts
# — a Japanese university's WordPress, the EIB, NHTSA. Both of the two
# re-tested by hand answered HTTP 200 immediately afterwards. A further ~100
# are `Connection reset by peer`, which looks like the upstream's own refusal
# and is not: curl reports HTTP 000 for the same hosts and the agent proxy names
# the cause itself, `ws_closed_mid_exchange`. The hosts are not denied by
# policy; it is the tunnel's capacity under many concurrent connections.
# So: the PAGE1_FAILED and NET_ERR rows in this file are NOT evidence that
# those sources are dead. The tool was changed after this run to retry such
# errors and report LOCAL_EGRESS when they persist, and those 828 rows were
# re-run at 4 jobs rather than 10 — docs/page-two-retry-2026-10-20.tsv.
# This is audit_cycle_health.py's lesson one layer up: a verdict that changes
# with the tool's own concurrency is not a measurement.
# WHAT SURVIVED, and what was done about it, is in the commits of 2026-10-20:
# 48 KKJ rows (a dead `Start` parameter, now a date-window cycle), 3 MET
# Malaysia rows, 2 Cabo Verde INE rows, 1 EU Parliament ceiling, 6 Setagaya
# layers recovered from a rename, 2 IDESCA San Carlos rows removed as withdrawn,
# and 14 WordPress rows that needed no change because the ENGINE was wrong
# about them rather than the rows.
